result_json.message: docs: revise plan 215 amendment and legacy recovery contracts
docs: add plan review for 215 implementation plan amendments

items.title: Define the mechanical scope of an authorize_amendment authorization and align --resolves with assessment references
items.reason: Registration must reject effects outside authorized scope, but authorize_amendment carries only rationale and findingRefs for one phase/observation (store.ts:640, implementation-recovery.ts:119-160). Meanwhile the plan lets an amendment invalidate earlier and completed phases, withdraw claims, and resolve findings across phases. --resolves is source-observation-only while the assessment allows phase-qualified refs, and reuse after the predecessor advances is unspecified.
items.failure: An authorization for one Phase-3 finding could, through reviewer assessment alone, reopen completed earlier phases and withdraw credit without operator consent; the scope check is unimplementable as written, and cross-phase resolutions can never match the source-only --resolves selector.
items.lowestCostCorrection: State that scope = binding, predecessor revision, source observation and findingRefs; --resolves must be a subset of those findingRefs (selector form aligned with the assessment); decide whether an earlier --from-phase or claim withdrawal needs additional typed operator consent; make authorizations single-use per predecessor revision; add a negative test for each out-of-scope effect.

items.title: Add routing.ts and sqlite-index.ts to Files Touched and the surface count
items.reason: The amendment override of the final_corrections shortcut must live in routing.ts (route derived at routing.ts:274-290). sqlite-index.ts independently re-derives implementation gate chains via deriveGateId, scans raw bindings for advisory mode, and projects observations, so revision-qualified gate fingerprints must be mirrored there.
items.failure: Without these, either Decision 4 reassessment routing is implemented outside the inventory or an index rebuild projects gate IDs that diverge from live store derivation, contradicting the success contract that a rebuild yields the same readiness.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Add both modules to the Files Touched table with their changes, attribute them to W3/W4, and update the production-file count from 30 to 32.

result_json.summary: The architecture (immutable binding plus appended revision fold, reviewer-assessed carry, retiring recover-plan while keeping historical decoding) is sound and matches the integrated code, including the existing atomicAppendIfAllNew CAS seam. One policy gap blocks: what a typed authorize_amendment authorizes is undefined, yet the plan allows earlier and completed phase invalidation, claim withdrawal and cross-phase resolution. Two inventory omissions (routing.ts, sqlite-index.ts) are mechanical.

baselineAssessment.reason: W1-W3 and W5 scores look reasonable; W4 (revision threading across admission, contexts, gates, decisions, corrections, routing, SQLite projection and completion) and W6 (archived-record upgrade discovery, all-delegation assets, two end-to-end lifecycles) each look closer to 8 than 5.

result_json.guidance: Operator approved extending typed authorize_amendment with structured scope: bind authorization to one predecessor revision; explicitly authorize earliest affected phase including completed-phase reopening; enumerate allowed claim withdrawals/edits and phase-qualified finding resolutions; consume authorization once; registration effects must fit both authorization and reviewer assessment. Preserve historical recovery acceptance under its former contract. Align CLI resolution selectors with qualified references. Fix routing.ts and sqlite-index.ts inventory omissions and surface estimate, then re-review.
